title: Staged traffic commitment and acceptance checklist for progressive experiments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: provide a prescriptive, engineer-friendly checklist and timeline for running progressive feature experiments (A/B, canary, and staged rollouts) that balance velocity with service reliability and user impact. Deliverable is a reusable "checklist + decision gates" artifact with instrumentation templates, alert thresholds, and a runbook for automated rollback and emergency mitigations.
milestones: M1 - Dry run & instrumentation (Week 0): validation of metrics, dashboard, and synthetic canary traffic against a shadow deployment.
M2 - Canary 1 (1% traffic, 24h): validate basic correctness, error rates, and latency; decision gate at 24h.
M3 - Canary 2 (5% traffic, 48h): validate load behavior, cache/KV patterns, and cost signals; decision gate at 48h.
M4 - Ramp (25% -> 75% over 72h): progressive ramps with automated gating and manual review checkpoints.
M5 - Full commit & postmortem (100% + 7d monitoring): finalize rollout and capture learnings and metrics drift analysis.
acceptance_criteria: No increase in 99th percentile tail latency > 15% relative to baseline for two consecutive buckets during each gate.
Error rate (5xx) increase not exceeding 0.02% absolute or 30% relative, whichever is smaller.
User-facing regression (as defined by product OKRs) limited to <1% of active users during Canary 2 window.
Feature correctness validated against smoke tests on 1000 sample requests with 0% critical failures.
Cost per 1k requests remains within expected bounds (±10%) given batching/quantization profile.
evaluation_metrics: Latency: p50/p95/p99 token-generation latency (ms) and end-to-end request latency.
Reliability: 5xx error rate, model timeouts, retry growth.
Quality: downstream evaluation metric (e.g., human-quality score or automated eval ROCI) and % of auto-fail prompts.
Cost: GPU-hours per 10k requests, tokens/time cost, and overall billing delta for the experiment cohort.
User signals: conversion funnel delta, retention delta, and support ticket volume for affected flows.
instrumentation_and_alerting: Create a dedicated dashboard in Metrics (link below) with gate-specific panels: latency percentiles, error types, traffic mix, and KV cache hit rate.
Set alert rules: (1) p99 latency spike > 15% sustained for 10 minutes -> P0 incident page; (2) 5xx spike > threshold -> automated rollback trigger.
Tag all experiment traffic with experiment_id and rollout_stage to enable sliceable telemetry and per-customer rollbacks.
Add tracing hooks to follow end-to-end request paths (client -> API -> model pool -> response) for triage of multi-component failures.
Pre-create a synthetic-canary job that runs representative prompts every 5 minutes to detect regressions before user exposure.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Shadow) - 48h: route mirrored traffic to new variant for passive observability. No user exposure.
Phase 1 (Canary 1) - 1% traffic, 24h: auto-check acceptance gates; hold for manual sign-off if any soft-warning triggers.
Phase 2 (Canary 2) - 5% traffic, 48h: run extended workloads including bursty patterns and long context sequences.
Phase 3 (Ramp) - 25% -> 75% over 72h: incremental increases every 6-12 hours with automated gate checks and a required PM/Eng sign-off at 50%.
Phase 4 (Commit) - 100% with 7d heightened monitoring and a scheduled postmortem within 10 days.
rollback_criteria_and_playbook: Automatic rollback triggers: p99 latency breach, sustained CPU/GPU queueing indicating overload, or 5xx spike beyond threshold.
Manual rollback triggers: user-impacting bug reports climbing > 3x baseline OR inability to meet correctness smoke tests.
Rollback steps: (1) flip traffic routing to previous stable model variant; (2) notify stakeholders via incident channel; (3) open hotfix ticket and label with 'rollback-followup'.
Post-rollback analysis: capture pre/post snapshots of telemetry, correlate with recent infra/serving changes, and schedule a root-cause review within 72h.
